statement: In mathematical optimization, a trust region is the subset of the region of an objective function that is approximated using a model function (often a quadratic), within which the step size is restricted so that the model is trusted only where it provides a reasonable approximation, with the region dynamically expanded or contracted based on the ratio of predicted improvement to actual improvement.

symbols.meaning: current estimate point in the domain of the objective function
expected improvement / predicted reduction in the cost function from the model approximation
actual improvement observed in the objective function, defined as f(x) - f(x + \Delta x)
parameter controlling the trust-region size (damping parameter)
matrix in the linear solver / quadratic approximation
right-hand side vector in the linear system A \Delta x = b
diagonal matrix with the same diagonal entries as matrix A

properties.why: The fit is evaluated by comparing the ratio of expected improvement from the model approximation to actual improvement observed in the objective function: \Delta f_{\text{pred}} / \Delta f_{\text{actual}}
If an adequate model of the objective function is found within the trust region, the region is expanded; conversely, if the approximation is poor, the region is contracted

If \Delta f_{\text{pred}} / \Delta f_{\text{actual}} > 0.5, the step is damped too much so the trust region is expanded (decrease \lambda); if the ratio is smaller than 0.25, the true function diverges too much from the model so the trust region is shrunk (increase \lambda)
Trust-region methods first choose a step size (trust-region size) and then a step direction, whereas line-search methods first choose a step direction and then a step size

Restricting the step size to prevent stepping too far is operationalized by solving (A + \lambda \operatorname{diag}(A)) \Delta x = b, geometrically adding a paraboloid centered at \Delta x = 0 to yield a smaller step

assumptions.assumption: The objective function can be approximated locally by a model function (often a quadratic surface)
assumptions.breaks_when: The objective function diverges substantially from the model surface within the region

assumptions.assumption: The actual improvement \Delta f_{\text{actual}} = f(x) - f(x + \Delta x) is non-zero when computing the fit evaluation ratio
assumptions.breaks_when: f(x + \Delta x) = f(x), leading to division by zero in \Delta f_{\text{pred}} / \Delta f_{\text{actual}}

assumptions.assumption: The step size is restricted to prevent stepping too far from the current estimate
assumptions.breaks_when: Steps are unconstrained and the initial guess is too far from the optimum, causing convergence to fail

failure_modes.cause: The trust region is too large, causing the true function to diverge too much from the model approximation
The trust-region size is too small (parameter \lambda is too large), damping the step excessively relative to actual reduction

failure_modes.signature: Failure to converge nicely when solving A \Delta x = b
failure_modes.cause: The initial guess is too far from the optimum and the step is not restricted to a trust region
